solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

flags: minor: A, B, D each contradict an explicit detail (no argument with lawyer; inventory is 'perfect'; narrator declines to describe letters), so elimination is quick
R007-01.notes: Narrator checks the ledger, finds the unrecorded shoebox of letters, and reconsiders the ledger as a 'disguise' rather than a straightforward self-portrait.

R007-02.notes: 'it seemed to me, even then' that recording every teacup price is about 'making sure no one can say she was careless' rather than easing anyone's job. C is the closest trap (incompleteness is learned later; at the time narrator found it 'perfect').

flags: minor: A (dressed) and D (outfitted) are near-synonyms from the same clothing sense of 'suit', so both eliminate together; 'agreed with' is slightly dated for 'suited' but clearly the best fit (cf. 'the climate agreed with me')
R007-03.notes: 'The work suited me' = was agreeable to/fit the narrator, as the next sentence (reliable notebook-keeper) confirms.

R007-04.notes: Kettle's date, price, and expected dent confirm ledger precision, setting up the shoebox omission in paragraph 3-4. C is a plausible trap since the kettle reappears at the end, but the kettle details do not explain that choice.

R007-05.notes: Standing, then sitting, then light changed white to orange and hours passed without the ledger: increasing absorption.

flags: minor: near-verbatim lift of 'for the envelopes were soft at the edges from handling' makes this a pure locate-and-match item

R007-07.notes: Inventory is accurate ('honest about every item') yet omits the letters the aunt valued most. B and D contradict the stated accuracy; C is unsupported.

flags: minor: answer substantially restates the keyed idea of R007-07 (record conceals while accurate); the two items reward the same inference and 07's stem helps answer 08
R007-08.notes: Narrator now sees a complete-seeming list as possibly a disguise and stops writing things down. B too strong (no contempt), C and D contradicted by ending.

R007-09.notes: Narrator was the family member with a notebook; after the discovery 'did not write down anything at all' marks a departure from that recording habit. A, B, D unsupported (narrator has yet to decide about the box; no imitation motive stated).
